enso.cpc_discussion: ENSO Alert System Status: El Niño Advisory   Synopsis:   El Niño continues to strengthen, with a strong-to-very strong El Niño likely through January-March 2027 (remaining greater than an 83% chance). El Niño strengthened further last month, with sea surface temperature anomalies exceeding +4.0°C in portions of the eastern equatorial Pacific [Fig. 1] . Most Niño indices increased in the past month, reaching +2.1°C in Niño-3.4, +3.0°C in Niño-3, and +3.9°C in Niño-1+2 [Fig. 2] . The equatorial subsurface temperature index (average from 180°-100°W) was well above average [Fig. 3] , reflecting a deeper-than-average thermocline. Subsurface temperatures remained in excess of +10.0°C at depth in the eastern Pacific Ocean [Fig. 4] . Low-level westerly wind anomalies and upper-level easterly wind anomalies stretched from the western to the east-central equatorial Pacific. Enhanced convection and rainfall persisted from the central to the eastern Pacific, while anomalies remained suppressed over Indonesia [Fig. 5] . The traditional and equatorial Southern Oscillation indices were significantly negative. Collectively, the coupled ocean-atmosphere system reflected a strengthening El Niño. The CPC Official ENSO outlook , which synthesizes multiple models from North America and abroad, indicates El Niño will continue to strengthen through the end of the year [Figs. 6 -7 -8] . notes: Wind/gust ranges: quantile-boosted models widened by a conformal margin fit on out-of-fold errors (days 1-10 ensemble model).

Temperature ranges: NBM high/low plus the empirical error distribution (by lead day and season) measured at Alamogordo, Holloman and Las Cruces airports; the same error spread is assumed at Hawk St, the Pass and Cloudcroft (mountain sites are not verified).
Rain: percentile amounts come from the hurdle model; coverage above nominal mostly reflects the large share of dry days. Cloudcroft days 8-10 slightly under-cover (88% vs 90%).
Test period: Jul 2025 – Oct 2026 (about 15 months), so coverage numbers carry a few points of sampling noise.

Area Forecast Discussion
National Weather Service El Paso TX/Santa Teresa NM
613 PM MDT Fri Oct 30 2026

...New AVIATION...


.KEY MESSAGES... Updated at 923 AM MDT Thu Oct 29 2026

 - Another round of thunderstorms spreading in from the west later
   tonight, with some areas at risk for flooding.
 
 - A quiet period looks to arrive in time for Halloween, Saturday.

 - A upper level system will bring more showers and thunderstorms to 
   the area Sunday afternoon into Monday morning.

 - Quieter and drier weather looks to prevail after Monday.

&&

.DISCUSSION...
Issued at 923 AM MDT Fri Oct 30 2026

After a cloudy, dry Friday morning and afternoon, another Pacific
shortwave will commence the next round of showers and 
thunderstorms from the west in the evening. The showers and 
thunderstorms could produce occasional periods of heavy rainfall 
and flash flooding, especially in Luna, Grant, and Hidalgo 
Counties in New Mexico. Showers and thunderstorms will continue 
well into the overnight hours until sunrise on All Hallow's Eve.

For what would be a Halloween Area Forecast Discussion, if the 
forecast was not a trick or a treat? Well, Halloween is expected 
to be a treat weather-wise, as a tiny shortwave ridge in between 
these shortwave troughs will bring dry air for prime trick-or- 
treating hours on Saturday. Skies will be partly cloudy and 
temperatures in the upper 60s/low 70s on Halloween.

As November begins and the clocks turn back an hour, the upper-
level trough and cold front will sweep through on Sunday. Showers
and thunderstorms will develop west of Deming in the afternoon at
a quick pace thanks to healthy mid-level winds, speeding through 
the region late Sunday night and into Monday morning. Showers
should move out by midday on Monday, and a drying trend begins 
through about next Friday. Temperatures early next week will be at
or slightly below normal.

&&

.AVIATION...
(00Z TAFS)
Issued at 606 PM MDT Fri Oct 30 2026

Showers are pushing eastward and will reach all TAF sites this
evening. A potential next round of rain possible after midnight
and looks more spotty. Should be dry by sunrise. BR and low cloud
bases will be possible around 3AM and should burn off soon after
sunrise. 


&&

.FIRE WEATHER...
Issued at 923 AM MDT Fri Oct 30 2026

Rain will enter the region from the west later this evening,
bringing the potential for flooding rains, but all the same, it
will keep fire weather conditions low. Min RHs today will be no
less than 45% for most of the region, and Saturday's min RHs will
be quite similar, even with a lull in the rain. Another round of
rain will sweep through on Sunday as a second trough moves 
through. Dry conditions return Monday afternoon. Ventilation rates
will improve from Poor today to Very Good on Sunday.

&&
